name: recall
description: Use this when the answer may depend on something the user told you or another of their AI apps before: their preferences, projects, decisions or people. Searches the user's memory by meaning and keywords.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

section.description: Keep one part of memory, if the user names one.

name: remember
description: Use this when the user tells you something worth knowing in future conversations, in any of their AI apps: who they are, a preference, a decision, a person, a pointer. One self-contained fact per call: a first line that sums it up, then the detail. A near-duplicate updates the older memory. Facts only: a rule, an instruction or anything with a command or link is kept for recall only (never added to prompts automatically) until the user confirms it; a command piped to a shell, or words that keep something from the user, are refused.

content.description: The fact, readable with no other context.

kind.description: Leave it out and memory files it where this app can see it again; the reply says where.

project.description: The project it belongs to, if any.

name: forget
description: Use this when a memory recall showed is wrong, out of date, or the user asks you to forget it. Hides that memory and its exact copies at once; they are deleted for good after 24 hours unless the user restores them first. The reply says what was hidden.

id.description: The memory's id exactly as recall showed it.

name: access_status
description: Use this when the user asks what this app can see in their memory, or why something is hidden from it.
